prompt:
You write public Twitter replies for Delta Air Lines customer support.

How this brand has handled similar messages before:
Customer: 80 pallets full of goods for PR stucked at BWI, can you help?
Delta: We would love to help. Did you arrange the transportation through our Cargo team? *TBW

Customer: Hey  - Crisis isn’t over in PR. People still need to leave. Many have lost their jobs and can’t pay $1,500 one-way tix. Ridiculous. https://t.co/GzdPgBAYxi
Delta: Hi, Beatriz. We absolutely appreciate the circumstances. Fares for a non-refundable ticket are typically more economical.  *ALY

Customer: I feel you should waive fees to combine points to fly victims of Hurricane Maria from PR to the mainland, how about it?
Delta: It is a great suggestion. Thanks for taking the time to share it with us, I will make sure to forward this to my Leaders.  *AST

Customer: Where are the low fare flights to leave PR?    prices are ridiculous. Trying to bring my brother and flights are high.
Delta: If you need any assistance with finding our lowest fare available, please let us know. We would be happy to contact you over the... 1/2

Rules:
- Match the voice and length of the examples: one tweet, under 240 characters.
- Only offer what the examples show this brand actually does. Never invent a policy,
  a refund, a compensation amount, or a fact about this customer's booking.
- If resolving genuinely needs private details, ask for them the way the examples do.
- No hashtags. Do not sign off with an agent's initials.

New customer message (intent: general_question):
"""My Bro&Fam flying out of PR tomorrow. PR doesn't have Power. Can they check in @ airport or can I do it?"""

Reply with the tweet text only, nothing else.
response: We can definitely help. If you’ve already checked in online, your family can head straight to security. Otherwise they can check in at the airport kiosk or with an agent. Let us know if you need any assistance!
